observed: cellWidth and measureAll (INPUTS mix): expected a full layout (5 rows) after setFixedCellWidth, M3 measured 1 (probe only)
correction: setFixedCellWidth no longer marks the kept sizes unusable in the harness
guard: the INPUTS scripts compare remeasured() exactly after every layout
lesson: a fixed cell width is not a measuring input of M3ListMeasure (sameInputs lists font, renderer, orientation, html.disable, label UI, preferred size, gap, text positions, alignments); write the expectation from that list, not from "every input"

observed: cellWidth/measureAll: expected a full layout, M3 measured 2 rows; an input toggled twice between two layouts (icon-text gap, html.disable, orientation) is back to its value at the last layout
correction: the harness snapshots the measuring inputs at every layout (identity, as sameInputs compares them) and expects a full layout only when the snapshot differs
guard: remeasured() exact after every layout of every script
lesson: derive "every row is measured" from the state at the last layout, not from the history of setter calls: a reverted change is no change

observed: refreshVisible, validateDescendants and validateReverse of M3VariableHeightLayoutCache executed 0 instructions in their own tests (all 281 tests passed); after the INVALID mix validateDescendants still executed 0
correction: new Mix.INVALID (expand/collapse + invalidations + stale sizes, no row-height changes) on the LARGE shape with variable row heights forced, and a getPreferredWidth comparison right after every invalidation; validateDescendants gets a deterministic scenario: load X, collapse X, expand its parent, invalidateSizes, collapse the parent
guard: REACH.tsv: every atom must execute in its own dynamic test
lesson: invalid sizes exist only after an invalidation, inside loaded subtrees that are collapsed, and only with variable row heights (inserted rows are measured at once); a passing differential is not proof that the atom ran: gate it by per-test coverage

observed: the declaration regex ran past the 120 s tool timeout on M3VariableHeightLayoutCache (nested quantifiers: a type class containing a space followed by \s+)
correction: the return-type class holds no space (generic arguments in these files have none)
guard: atomizer finishes in < 1 s over the 10 files
lesson: a regex over source text must not let two adjacent quantified classes share a character; match lexically, not by backtracking

observed: 11 atoms UNCLASSIFIED: the 10 constructors and M3ExpandedState.removeDescendants
correction: constructors (name == owner) are INITIAL_STATE; removeDescendants joins ADD_REMOVE_GET
guard: the atomizer fails on any UNCLASSIFIED atom
lesson: a constructor's contract is the state a new instance answers plus its argument checks: its own pattern

observed: display names unique per owner collided inside one file: Host.sort and M3SorterLanes.sort are both sort()
correction: names are unique per test class; a name shared by two owners of one file is qualified with the nested owner (Host.sort)
guard: oneTestPerAtom in every generated class: distinct display names == census atoms
lesson: the unit of uniqueness is the generated file, not the declaring type

observed: java could not start: '--add-opens a=b --add-opens c=d' split into tokens and sorted with sort -u

correction: -XX:+DisplayVMOutputToStderr: VM output to perf_<pkg>.comp, PERF lines alone in perf_<pkg>.log

observed: the first OperatingSystemMXBean.getCpuLoad() read 0.0 or 100.0 (no previous sample)
correction: prime the bean, then sample over 500 ms of this JVM sleeping: the load of the other sessions
guard: LOAD start/warm/end in every perf log
lesson: a load figure needs a sampling interval

correction: note FOLDED below 0.1 ns (no measurement); tier4_deopt counts only tier-4 compilations made not entrant; loop_tier reports the tier of the measured loop that inlines the atom
guard: PERF.tsv header explains tier, loop_tier, tier4_deopt and FOLDED
lesson: report what the JIT did with the loop, not only with the method

guard: diff -r of test/jdk/sun/swing before and after: identical
lesson: generated files and their templates both carry the licence; write escape-heavy code with Write/Edit, never through a shell heredoc
